question: Should OpenClaw surface channel delivery failures to agents through system events, message-tool result status, or another shared delivery outcome contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes shared agent/channel semantics, retry expectations, transcript state, and plugin-facing behavior, so automation should not choose the product/API contract unilaterally.

options.title: Define a shared delivery outcome contract
options.body: Choose a generic agent/channel contract first, then implement final-reply and direct-send failure reporting against that single source of truth.

options.title: Use system-event injection
options.body: Treat failed channel delivery as a sanitized session-scoped system event, accepting prompt-context and retry-semantics changes as the product direction.

options.title: Keep fixes scoped to callers
options.body: Limit work to CLI, cron, and channel-specific status surfaces, leaving broad agent-visible final-reply failure notification out of core for now.

recommendation.title: Define a shared delivery outcome contract
recommendation.body: Choose a generic agent/channel contract first, then implement final-reply and direct-send failure reporting against that single source of truth.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest recent history match for the current deliveryStatus, channel/outbound, and final reply routing surfaces.
